question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution stipulates that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 141.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 141 of the Indian Constitution states that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India. (अनुच्छेद 141 — सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा घोषित विधि)

 

• This provision gives the Supreme Court's decisions the force of a binding precedent on all subordinate and High Courts across the country, ensuring uniformity in the interpretation of law.

 

• Article 141 falls under Part V (The Union), Chapter IV — The Union Judiciary of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 137 empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgments; Article 143 deals with its advisory jurisdiction.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 140 (Option 2): Empowers Parliament to confer supplementary powers on the Supreme Court that are not inconsistent with the Constitution.

 

• Article 142 (Option 3): Empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any matter pending before it.

 

• Article 145 (Option 4): Deals with the Supreme Court's rule-making power regarding its own procedure.

question: Who among the following Sultans of Delhi started the system of Sijda and Paibos?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghiyas ud din Balban.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghiyas ud din Balban, a Sultan of the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty of Delhi, introduced the court ceremonies of Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the ruler's feet) to enhance the prestige and authority of the crown. (सिजदा और पैबोस — ग़यासुद्दीन बलबन)

 

• Balban ruled Delhi from 1266 to 1287 CE and is known for reorganising the military department (Diwan-i-Arz) and crushing the power of the Chahalgani (Group of Forty nobles).

 

• He believed in the theory of kingship and projected the Sultan as the 'Shadow of God' (Zil-i-Ilahi) on earth, adopting an elaborate and rigid court etiquette.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balban also established a strong espionage system (barid) and maintained a large, well-organised army to defend the Delhi Sultanate against Mongol invasions.

 

NOTE

 

• Muhammad Bin Tughluq (Option 1): Known for the transfer of capital to Daulatabad and introduction of token currency.

 

• Nasir ud din Muhammad (Option 2): Balban's predecessor's son; ruled as a pious, weak Sultan while Balban held actual power as Naib.

 

• Qutb ud-Din Aibak (Option 4): Founder of the Slave Dynasty; began construction of the Qutub Minar and Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.

question: Someity is related to which of the following events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tokyo paralympic 2020.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Someity was the official mascot of the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games. (सोमेइटी शुभंकर — टोक्यो पैरालंपिक 2020)

 

• The name is a play on the words 'so mighty' and someiyoshino, a popular variety of Japanese cherry blossom, reflecting both physical strength and Japanese culture.

 

• Someity has cherry-blossom-inspired pink antenna-like sensors that convey powers and represent the strength of Para athletes.

 

• The Tokyo 2020 Olympic mascot (a separate character) was named Miraitowa, chosen through a nationwide vote among Japanese schoolchildren along with Someity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tokyo 2020 Games (Olympics and Paralympics) were postponed to 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic but retained the '2020' branding.

 

NOTE

 

• Tokyo Olympics 2020 (Option 1): Its mascot was Miraitowa, not Someity.

 

• Winter Olympics 2022 (Option 2): Held in Beijing, China; mascot was Bing Dwen Dwen.

 

• Commonwealth Games 2022 (Option 3): Held in Birmingham, England; mascot was Perry the Bull.

question: Pandit Kishan Maharaj of Benaras Gharana was a ________ player.
solution_text:
The correct answer is tabla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Kishan Maharaj was a legendary tabla player belonging to the Benaras (Varanasi) Gharana of tabla playing. (किशन महाराज — तबला वादक, बनारस घराना)

 

• He was renowned for his mastery of laya (rhythm) and made significant contributions to popularising tabla as a solo concert instrument.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to Indian classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Benaras Gharana of tabla is known for its powerful, resonant strokes (bol) and is one of the six major tabla gharanas, alongside Delhi, Ajrada, Lucknow, Farukhabad and Punjab.

 

NOTE

 

• Santoor (Option 1): Associated with maestros like Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.

 

• Flute (Option 2): Associated with maestros like Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia.

 

• Sarangi (Option 3): Associated with maestros like Ustad Sultan Khan and Pandit Ram Narayan.

question: Identify the last element from the fifth period.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Xenon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fifth period of the modern periodic table runs from Rubidium (Rb, atomic number 37) to Xenon (Xe, atomic number 54). (क्सीनन — पांचवीं आवर्त का अंतिम तत्व)

 

• Xenon is a noble gas (Group 18) and is the last, i.e. the 18th element, of the fifth period.

 

• The fifth period contains 18 elements in total, including the 4d transition series (Yttrium to Cadmium).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Elements of Period 6 end at Radon (Rn), another noble gas, while Period 2 and 3 end at Neon (Ne) and Argon (Ar) respectively — each period conventionally ends with a noble gas (except Period 1, which ends at Helium, and Period 7).

 

NOTE

 

• Helium (Option 1): The noble gas that ends Period 1, not Period 5.

 

• Yttrium (Option 2): A transition metal that begins the 4d series within Period 5, not its last element.

 

• Rubidium (Option 3): The first element (alkali metal) of Period 5, not the last.

question: The largest freshwater lake of India is ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wular.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Wular Lake, located in the Bandipora district of Jammu & Kashmir, is the largest freshwater lake in India. (वुलर झील — भारत की सबसे बड़ी मीठे पानी की झील)

 

• It is formed by the Jhelum River and is believed to be of tectonic origin, having formed due to tectonic activity in the region.

 

• Wular Lake is a designated Ramsar site (Wetland of International Importance), recognised for its rich biodiversity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vembanad Lake (Kerala) is the longest lake in India, while Chilika Lake (Odisha) is the largest brackish/saltwater lagoon in India and the largest coastal lagoon in the country.

 

NOTE

 

• Chilika (Option 1): A brackish-water lagoon in Odisha, the largest coastal lagoon in India, not a freshwater lake.

 

• Koleru (Option 2): A freshwater lake in Andhra Pradesh, but much smaller than Wular; known as a major bird sanctuary.

 

• Vembanad (Option 3): A brackish-water lake in Kerala; it is the longest lake in India but not the largest freshwater lake.

question: Which of the following rights is guaranteed by Article 25 of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to freedom of religion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 25 of the Indian Constitution guarantees freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health and other provisions of Part III. (अनुच्छेद 25 — धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार)

 

• It is one of the provisions under the Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28) guaranteed to all persons, not just citizens, in India.

 

• This right is subject to reasonable restrictions that the State can impose in the interest of public order, morality and health.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 26 grants religious denominations the freedom to manage their own religious affairs; Article 27 prohibits taxes for promotion of any particular religion; Article 28 deals with freedom from attending religious instruction in certain educational institutions.

 

NOTE

 

• Cultural and educational rights (Option 2): Guaranteed under Articles 29-30, protecting the interests of minorities.

 

• Right to equality (Option 3): Guaranteed under Articles 14-18.

 

• Right to constitutional remedies (Option 4): Guaranteed under Article 32, described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

question: Which water body separates Andaman in the north and Nicobar in the south?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ten Degree Channel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman Islands (to the north) from the Nicobar Islands (to the south) in the Bay of Bengal. (टेन डिग्री चैनल — अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह)

 

• It is named after its approximate location along the 10th parallel north latitude and is about 150 km wide.

 

• The Andaman and Nicobar group comprises around 572 islands, of which only a small fraction are inhabited.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Eight Degree Channel separates the Lakshadweep and Minicoy islands, while the Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the rest of the Lakshadweep islands.

 

NOTE

 

• Eight Degree Channel (Option 2): Separates Minicoy Island from the Maldives, unrelated to Andaman-Nicobar.

 

• Eleven Degree Channel (Option 3): Separates the Lakshadweep islands (Amindivi group) from the Minicoy island, again in the Lakshadweep archipelago.

 

• Nine Degree Channel (Option 4): Separates Minicoy Island from the Amindivi group of the Lakshadweep islands.

question: On 30 January 2023, the two-day meeting of the first International Financial Architecture Working Group of G-20, being held under the chairmanship of India, was inaugurated by the Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Narendra Singh Tomar and Minister of Food Processing Industries, Pashupati Kumar Paras in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandigarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first meeting of the G20 International Financial Architecture Working Group (IFA-WG), held under India's G20 Presidency, took place on 30-31 January 2023 in Chandigarh. (चंडीगढ़ — G20 वित्तीय वास्तुकला बैठक)

 

• The two-day meeting was inaugurated by Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Narendra Singh Tomar and Minister of Food Processing Industries Pashupati Kumar Paras.

 

• The IFA-WG discusses issues such as global economic outlook, capital flows, sovereign debt vulnerabilities, and reforms to the international financial architecture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India held the G20 Presidency from 1 December 2022 to 30 November 2023, culminating in the G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi in September 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhubaneswar (Option 1): Hosted other G20-related meetings but not this particular IFA-WG session.

 

• New Delhi (Option 2): Hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in September 2023, not this January 2023 working group meeting.

 

• Mumbai (Option 3): Hosted several G20 finance-track meetings but not the first IFA-WG meeting.

question: Who among the following Mauryan rulers conquered Kalinga?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashoka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ashoka, the third Mauryan emperor, conquered Kalinga (present-day coastal Odisha) in 261 BCE, in one of the bloodiest wars of ancient India. (अशोक — कलिंग युद्ध)

 

• The immense bloodshed and suffering of the Kalinga War led Ashoka to renounce armed conquest and embrace Buddhism, adopting the policy of Dhamma Vijaya (conquest through righteousness).

 

• Details of the war and Ashoka's remorse are recorded in his 13th Major Rock Edict.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ashoka's edicts were deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837 and were mostly written in the Brahmi script (with Kharosthi, Aramaic and Greek in the northwest).

 

NOTE

 

• Bindusara (Option 2): Ashoka's father, second Mauryan ruler, known as 'Amitraghata'; expanded the empire in the Deccan.

 

• Brihadratha (Option 3): The last Mauryan ruler, assassinated by his general Pushyamitra Shunga in 185 BCE, ending the Mauryan dynasty.

 

• Chandragupta Maurya (Option 4): Founder of the Mauryan Empire; defeated Seleucus Nicator and later became a Jain monk under Bhadrabahu.

question: The term 'Straight drive' is related to which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cricket.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'straight drive' is a classical batting shot in Cricket, played with a vertical bat, sending the ball back straight past the bowler towards the sight screen. (स्ट्रेट ड्राइव — क्रिकेट)

 

• It is considered one of the most elegant and technically demanding shots, requiring precise timing and full extension of the bat.

 

• Other cricketing shots include the cover drive, square cut, pull, hook, and sweep.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cricket terminology also includes terms like 'silly point', 'googly', 'yorker' and 'duck', each describing a specific fielding position, delivery type or dismissal.

 

NOTE

 

• Hockey (Option 1): Uses terms like 'penalty corner', 'dribbling' and 'bully'.

 

• Football (Option 3): Uses terms like 'offside', 'free kick' and 'header'.

 

• Badminton (Option 4): Uses terms like 'smash', 'drop shot' and 'let'.

question: Which organic compound has a pleasant almond aroma that is commonly used to impart almond flavour to chocolate and baked goods?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Benzaldehyde.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Benzaldehyde is an organic aromatic compound with a characteristic pleasant almond-like aroma, and is commonly used as an artificial almond flavouring agent in chocolates and baked goods. (बेंजाल्डिहाइड — बादाम जैसी सुगंध)

 

• It occurs naturally in bitter almonds as a breakdown product of amygdalin and has the chemical formula C6H5CHO.

 

• Benzaldehyde is also used industrially as a precursor in the production of dyes, perfumes, and other flavouring compounds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common food-flavouring esters/aldehydes include ethyl butyrate (pineapple), isoamyl acetate (banana), and ethyl maltol (cotton candy/caramel).

 

NOTE

 

• Manzanate (Option 1): Not a standard recognised flavour compound associated with almond aroma.

 

• Ethyl maltol (Option 3): Produces a sweet, cotton-candy/caramel-like aroma, not almond.

 

• Isoamyl acetate (Option 4): Produces a banana-like aroma, used to flavour banana-scented products.

question: शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Net National Product) क्या होता है (what is it)?
option_1: सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Gross National Product) और मूल्यह्रास (depreciation) का गुणनफल (product/multiplication) शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Net National Product) होता है।
option_2: सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Gross National Product) और विदेशियों की आय (income of foreigners) का योग (sum) शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Net National Product) होता है।
option_3: शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Net National Product) सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Gross National Product) के बराबर (equal) होता है।
option_4: सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Gross National Product) और मूल्यह्रास (depreciation) का अंतर (difference) शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Net National Product) होता है।
solution_text:
The correct answer is सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Gross National Product) और मूल्यह्रास (depreciation) का अंतर (difference) शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Net National Product) होता है।

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Net National Product (NNP) = Gross National Product (GNP) − Depreciation. Depreciation refers to the wear and tear of capital assets during the production process. (शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद — सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद घटा मूल्यह्रास)

 

• GNP measures the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a country's residents (both within the country and abroad) in a year, including net income from abroad.

 

• Subtracting depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) from GNP gives the net measure, NNP, which reflects the actual addition to a nation's wealth after accounting for capital consumed.

 

• NNP is also known as the National Income at market prices when measured for a nation as a whole.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NNP at factor cost (obtained by subtracting net indirect taxes from NNP at market price) is the standard measure of a country's National Income.

 

• GDP (Gross Domestic Product) differs from GNP in that it excludes net income from abroad and measures only domestic production.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrect — NNP is obtained by subtracting, not multiplying, depreciation from GNP.

 

• Option 2: Incorrect — adding foreigners' income to GNP does not yield NNP; in fact GNP itself already includes net income from abroad.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect — NNP is always less than GNP (by the amount of depreciation), so the two cannot be equal.

question:
Match the columns.

Column-A (Enzyme/Protein): i. Helicase  ii. RNA primase  iii. DNA polymerase  iv. DNA ligase

Column-B (Role in DNA replication): a. Joins the 3' end of the new DNA fragment to the 5' end of the previous one  b. Nucleotide polymerisation  c. RNA primer synthesis  d. Opens up the DNA double helix
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Helicase (i) unwinds and opens up the DNA double helix (d) by breaking the hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs ahead of the replication fork. (हेलिकेज़ एंजाइम — डीएनए द्विकुंडली को खोलना)

 

• RNA primase (ii) synthesises a short RNA primer (c), providing the free 3'-OH group needed for DNA polymerase to begin synthesis.

 

• DNA polymerase (iii) carries out nucleotide polymerisation (b), adding complementary nucleotides to extend the new DNA strand in the 5'→3' direction.

 

• DNA ligase (iv) seals the gaps between Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand by joining the 3' end of a new DNA fragment to the 5' end of the previous one (a).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• On the lagging strand, DNA is synthesised discontinuously as short Okazaki fragments, which are later joined together by DNA ligase to form a continuous strand.

 

• DNA replication is described as semi-conservative, as demonstrated by the Meselson-Stahl experiment.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d): Incorrectly assigns Helicase to ligation and DNA ligase to unwinding the helix.

 

• Option 2 (i-b, ii-a, iii-d, iv-c): Incorrectly assigns Helicase to polymerisation and RNA primase to unwinding the double helix.

 

• Option 4 (i-b, ii-c, iii-a, iv-d): Incorrectly assigns Helicase to nucleotide polymerisation instead of unwinding the DNA double helix.

question: सिख, बंदी छोड़ दिवस (Bandi Chhor Divas — the day of release of prisoners) मनाते हैं (celebrate) जो किस हिंदू त्योहार (Hindu festival) के साथ मेल खाता है (coincides with)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is दिवाली (Diwali).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bandi Chhor Divas ('Day of Release of Prisoners') is celebrated by Sikhs on the same day as the Hindu festival of दिवाली (Diwali). (बंदी छोड़ दिवस — दिवाली)

 

• It commemorates the release of the sixth Sikh Guru, Guru Hargobind Sahib, along with 52 Hindu kings, from imprisonment at Gwalior Fort by the Mughal Emperor Jahangir.

 

• Sikhs mark the occasion by lighting up Gurdwaras, most notably the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) in Amritsar, which is illuminated with lamps and fireworks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Hargobind Sahib is also remembered for introducing the concept of 'Miri-Piri' — the combination of temporal (worldly) and spiritual authority in Sikh leadership.

 

NOTE

 

• Ganesh Chaturthi (Option 1): A Hindu festival celebrating the birth of Lord Ganesha, unrelated to Bandi Chhor Divas.

 

• Holi (Option 2): The Hindu festival of colours, celebrated in spring, unrelated to Bandi Chhor Divas.

 

• Dussehra (Option 4): Marks the victory of Lord Rama over Ravana (or Durga over Mahishasura), celebrated separately from Bandi Chhor Divas/Diwali.

question: Under the PL 480 scheme, India used to import wheat from which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is USA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the PL 480 (Public Law 480) scheme, also known as the 'Food for Peace' programme, India imported wheat from the United States of America (USA). (पीएल 480 योजना — संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका से गेहूं आयात)

 

• The scheme was enacted by the US Congress in 1954 to provide food aid, including surplus agricultural commodities, to food-deficit countries like India, especially through the 1950s and 1960s.

 

• Heavy dependence on PL 480 wheat imports was one of the factors that spurred India to launch the Green Revolution in the mid-1960s to achieve food self-sufficiency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution in India, led by scientists like M.S. Swaminathan, introduced high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers and irrigation, primarily boosting wheat production in states like Punjab and Haryana.

 

NOTE

 

• USSR (Option 1): India had trade and defence cooperation with the USSR, but the PL 480 food aid scheme was specifically a US programme.

 

• France (Option 3) and UK (Option 4): Neither country was the source of PL 480 wheat imports; PL 480 was exclusively a US legislative programme.

question: Which crop is grown during the Zaid season in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cucumber.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Zaid season is a short cropping season between the Rabi and Kharif seasons, roughly from March to June, and cucumber is a major crop grown during this period. (जायद फसल — खीरा)

 

• Zaid crops are typically grown on irrigated land and include watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, and vegetable/fodder crops that require warm, dry weather and irrigation.

 

• These crops have a short growing duration and help utilise agricultural land between the two major cropping seasons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important Zaid crops include watermelon, muskmelon, moong (green gram), and vegetables like pumpkin, bitter gourd and bottle gourd.

 

NOTE

 

• Jowar (Option 2) and Bajra (Option 3): Major Kharif (monsoon season, June-October) crops.

 

• Maize (Option 4): Primarily grown as a Kharif crop in India, though it can also be grown in Rabi and Zaid seasons in some regions; it is not the characteristic Zaid crop.

question: Kalakshetra style is associated with which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kalakshetra style is a distinct style of Bharatanatyam, developed by Rukmini Devi Arundale, who founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai (Adyar) in 1936. (कलाक्षेत्र शैली — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• The Kalakshetra style is known for its emphasis on geometric precision, clean lines, and disciplined technique, and for adapting the dance form to make it more accessible and respectable in modern society.

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale reformed Bharatanatyam from its earlier Sadir/Devadasi tradition into a codified classical art form performed on the proscenium stage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu and is regarded as one of the oldest of the eight classical dance forms of India, traditionally associated with temple worship.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 1): Classical dance of Odisha, notable exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

• Kathak (Option 2): Classical dance of North India, associated with gharanas like Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 3): Classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, originating as a dance-drama tradition.

question: When and at which place did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is On 13 April 1919, at Amritsar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 (the day of Baisakhi) at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, Punjab. (जलियांवाला बाग हत्याकांड — 13 अप्रैल 1919, अमृतसर)

 

• British troops under General Reginald Dyer opened fire without warning on an unarmed crowd of men, women and children gathered peacefully to protest the Rowlatt Act and the arrest of leaders Dr. Satyapal and Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew.

 

• Hundreds of people were killed and over a thousand were injured in the massacre, making it one of the most brutal episodes of British colonial rule in India.

 

• The massacre led Rabindranath Tagore to renounce his Knighthood in protest, and significantly intensified the Indian independence movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The massacre led to the setting up of the Hunter Commission to inquire into the incident, and inspired the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920) by Mahatma Gandhi.

 

• Udham Singh later assassinated Michael O'Dwyer (the then Lieutenant Governor of Punjab) in London in 1940, in retaliation for the massacre.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (12 April 1919, at Chauri Chaura): Incorrect date and location — Chauri Chaura was the site of a 1922 incident during the Non-Cooperation Movement, unrelated to Jallianwala Bagh.

 

• Option 3 (13 May 1918, at Amritsar): Incorrect date/year — the massacre occurred in 1919, not 1918.

 

• Option 4 (14 March 1919, at Amritsar): Incorrect date — the massacre occurred on 13 April 1919.

question: V Satyanarayana Sarma, a Padma Shri awardee, was recognised for which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• V. Satyanarayana Sarma (Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma) was a renowned exponent of the Kuchipudi classical dance form, particularly celebrated for his portrayal of female roles (Stree Vesham). (वी सत्यनारायण शर्मा — कुचिपुड़ी नृत्य)

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri by the Government of India for his contribution to Kuchipudi dance.

 

• He belonged to the Vedantam family of Kuchipudi village, Andhra Pradesh, a lineage traditionally associated with preserving and teaching the Kuchipudi dance-drama tradition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kuchipudi originated as a dance-drama form in the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh, traditionally performed by male Brahmin artists, including in female roles.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 1): Classical dance of Odisha; notable exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 2): Classical dance of Tamil Nadu; notable exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

• Kathak (Option 3): Classical dance of North India; notable exponents include Birju Maharaj.

question: Which of the following cities of Nepal does NOT have a branch of 'Indian Citizen's Association of Nepal'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lalitpur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Citizen's Association of Nepal does not have a branch in Lalitpur; its branches are located in cities such as Pokhara, Bhairahawa and Damak, among others. (भारतीय नागरिक संघ, नेपाल — ललितपुर में शाखा नहीं)

 

• The association works for the welfare of Indian citizens residing in Nepal, providing support and representing their interests locally.

 

• This is a specific, exam-based fact regarding the organisational branch network of the association across various Nepalese cities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nepal shares an open border with India, and a large number of Indian citizens live and work across various Nepalese towns and cities under bilateral arrangements like the Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• Pokhara, Bhairahawa and Damak (Options 1, 3, 4): Each of these cities does have a branch of the Indian Citizen's Association of Nepal, unlike Lalitpur.

question: In February 2022, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare announced the launch of ________, which is a doorstep distribution drive to deliver crop insurance policies to farmers under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meri Policy Mere Hath.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In February 2022, the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare launched 'Meri Policy Mere Hath', a doorstep distribution drive to deliver crop insurance policy documents to farmers under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY). (मेरी पॉलिसी मेरे हाथ — पीएमएफबीवाई)

 

• The initiative aimed to ensure that every insured farmer physically receives their policy document, improving transparency and farmer awareness under PMFBY.

 

• PMFBY was launched in 2016 to provide comprehensive crop insurance coverage against yield losses due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMFBY is implemented on a voluntary basis for all farmers (since 2020) and is administered by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

 

NOTE

 

• Saubhagya scheme (Option 2): A scheme for universal household electrification, launched in 2017.

 

• SEED scheme (Option 3): Relates to certification and distribution of quality seeds to farmers, not a doorstep policy-delivery drive.

 

• Kaushal Yojana (Option 4): Refers to skill-development initiatives like the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, unrelated to crop insurance.

question: In which of the following states Vidhan Sabha elections was not held in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

• In 2022, Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly) elections were not held in Haryana — the state's last assembly election was in 2019, with the next due in 2024. (हरियाणा — 2022 में विधानसभा चुनाव नहीं)

 

• In 2022, assembly elections were held in five states: Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa, and Manipur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

• Punjab (Option 3): Held assembly elections in February 2022; AAP won a decisive majority.

question: Who designed the administrative code to separate revenue administration from judicial administration?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Cornwallis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Cornwallis, Governor-General of India (1786-1793), designed the administrative/judicial code (Cornwallis Code, 1793) that separated revenue administration from judicial administration. (लॉर्ड कार्नवालिस — कार्नवालिस संहिता 1793)

 

• Under this reform, District Collectors were stripped of their judicial and magisterial powers, which were transferred to separate District Judges/Magistrates, establishing the principle of separation of powers in colonial administration.

 

• Cornwallis is also known for introducing the Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) of land revenue in Bengal in 1793, and for reorganising the civil services and the police system in British India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cornwallis is often referred to as the 'Father of Civil Services in India' for his reforms in recruitment and administration of the covenanted civil service.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Lytton (Option 1): Known for the Vernacular Press Act (1878) and the Second Anglo-Afghan War.

 

• Lord Auckland (Option 3): Known for the First Anglo-Afghan War (1839-42).

 

• Warren Hastings (Option 4): First Governor-General of Bengal; introduced the Regulating Act, 1773 administrative framework and the earlier Judicial Plan of 1772, but it was Cornwallis who formally separated revenue and judicial functions.

question: Identify the correct statement about Newlands' law of octaves.
option_1: He started with the element having the highest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at thorium which was the 56th element.
option_2: He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at sodium.
option_3: He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at aluminium.
option_4: He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at thorium which was the 56th element.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at thorium which was the 56th element.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• John Newlands' Law of Octaves (1866) arranged the then-known elements in order of increasing atomic mass, starting from hydrogen (lowest atomic mass) and ending at thorium, the 56th element in his arrangement. (न्यूलैंड्स का अष्टक नियम — हाइड्रोजन से थोरियम तक)

 

• Newlands observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, resembling the octaves of Western music, hence the name 'Law of Octaves'.

 

• The law worked reasonably well for lighter elements but broke down after calcium, as it did not leave room for undiscovered elements, and did not hold for heavier elements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newlands' work laid important groundwork for later, more successful classifications, particularly Dmitri Mendeleev's Periodic Table (1869), which arranged elements by atomic mass while leaving gaps for undiscovered elements.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrect — Newlands started with the element of the lowest, not highest, atomic mass (hydrogen has the lowest atomic mass of all elements).

 

• Option 2: Incorrect — his arrangement ended at thorium, not sodium; sodium is a much lighter element positioned early in the sequence.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect — his arrangement ended at thorium, not aluminium; aluminium is also a lighter element positioned early in the sequence.
